findings.claim: The row's rear-seam driver is a Hebrew form-class claim about MT 57:14 that is carried on the English witness alone: no pointed splice and no oshb:Isa.57.14 entry in boundary_evidence_refs.
findings.grounds: The row closes at web:Isa.57.13 because of 'the third-person messenger introduction “He will say” that opens a fresh unit at web:Isa.57.14' — a form-class label ('third-person messenger introduction') on Hebrew that is never quoted. MT 57:14 opens verse-initially on וְאָמַ֥ר (oshb:Isa.57.14, byte tier), the 3ms speech verb that carries the claim; boundary_evidence_refs lists web:Isa.57.14 but no oshb:Isa.57.14, although the same list carries oshb refs for 57:3, 57:4, 57:6, 57:7, 57:13 and 57:15. The claim is byte-TRUE; the defect is the missing engagement, and the book-order neighbor row does splice that verb at byte tier at its own front seam.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): splice וְאָמַ֥ר (oshb:Isa.57.14, byte tier) into boundary_rationale beside the existing WEB citation and add oshb:Isa.57.14 to boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: The in-span form-class claim at 57:5 — the ground on which the row declines to cut at the masculine-plural/feminine-singular turn — is asserted against a web: ref with no pointed splice of the participles it names.
findings.grounds: The row states 'No finite second-person form appears at web:Isa.57.5, a participial chain describing the ritual acts rather than addressing anyone directly.' The positive half of that claim is spliceable and is not spliced: MT 57:5 opens on הַנֵּֽחָמִים֙ (oshb:Isa.57.5, byte tier) and carries a second participle at שֹׁחֲטֵ֤י (oshb:Isa.57.5, byte tier). The absence claim itself re-derives as true from the verse's own bytes, but the row attaches a Hebrew form claim to a WEB reference only.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: splice הַנֵּֽחָמִים֙ and שֹׁחֲטֵ֤י (oshb:Isa.57.5, byte tier) beside the form claim and cite the MT witness for it.

findings.claim: The cross-seam device pair in device_notes is labelled with a blended role name and an inaccurate positional description of the in-span occurrence.
findings.grounds: device_notes calls the pair 'the lofty-epithet form' and locates the first member as 'closing this row's own front descriptor', but וְנִשָּׂ֔א (oshb:Isa.57.7, byte tier) stands mid-span inside עַ֤ל הַר גָּבֹ֨הַּ֙ וְנִשָּׂ֔א (oshb:Isa.57.7, byte tier), an attributive adjective modifying the mountain — not an epithet and not at the row's front — while only וְנִשָּׂ֗א (oshb:Isa.57.15, byte tier) is the divine epithet. The tier and digit re-derive correctly (byte tier: 1 verse; accent-stripped tier: 6 verses — Isa 2:2, 6:1, 39:6, 52:13, 57:7, 57:15), and the count object is honestly named as 'the form', but the 6-verse set mixes both roles without that being said.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: name the two roles separately (attributive adjective of the mountain at oshb:Isa.57.7 vs divine epithet at oshb:Isa.57.15), drop 'front descriptor' for the span-internal occurrence, and say that the accent-stripped 6-verse form count spans both roles.

findings.claim: The row's span-cohesion warrant — that first-person-plural verb forms continue through web:Isa.59.9-Isa.59.14 — overreaches its own bytes by two verses.
findings.grounds: The last first-person-plural verb in the span is יְדַֽעֲנֽוּם (oshb:Isa.59.12, byte tier). MT 59:13 carries no finite first-person form at all: פָּשֹׁ֤עַ וְכַחֵשׁ֙ (oshb:Isa.59.13, byte tier) and הֹר֧וֹ וְהֹג֛וֹ (oshb:Isa.59.13, byte tier) are infinitives absolute, and its only first-person element is the suffix on אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ (oshb:Isa.59.13, byte tier). MT 59:14 carries no first-person form of any kind — וְהֻסַּ֤ג אָחוֹר֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט (oshb:Isa.59.14, byte tier) opens a third-person summary that runs to the verse's close at וּנְכֹחָ֖ה לֹא תוּכַ֥ל לָבֽוֹא (oshb:Isa.59.14, byte tier). Both seams survive independently (the voice shift at MT 59:9 and the wayyiqtol onset at MT 59:15), so the boundary is not moved by this.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: restrict the first-person-plural form claim to web:Isa.59.9-Isa.59.12 and argue 59:13-59:14 on their own ground (the infinitive-absolute catalogue of the confession's own transgressions at MT 59:13 and the third-person summary at MT 59:14 standing before the wayyiqtol onset).

findings.claim: The device_notes bracket mis-states where the no-justice phrase stands in MT 59:8: it is mid-verse, not verse-closing.
findings.grounds: device_notes calls וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier) 'the no-justice phrase closing the verse just before this row's own front seam'. In MT 59:8 that phrase stands as the fourth and fifth of sixteen tokens, immediately before the athnach at בְּמַעְגְּלוֹתָ֑ם (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier); the verse actually closes on לֹ֥א יָדַ֖ע שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier). The partner claim is correct — אֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּֽט (oshb:Isa.59.15, byte tier) does close MT 59:15 — and both digits re-derive (skeleton tier: 2 verses, Isa 59:8 and 59:15; the justice noun at skeleton tier: 40 verses book-wide, 5 in this chapter).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: state the MT 59:8 occurrence as mid-verse (before that verse's own caesura) rather than verse-closing, keeping the two digits as swept.

findings.claim: device_notes carries schema/administrative register in row prose.
findings.grounds: device_notes opens 'The oss tag here names the nearest taxonomy class for what is, precisely, a grammatical PERSON/voice shift ... rather than a change of addressee' — the row narrating its own field name and its taxonomy fit rather than the substrate. The underlying disclosure is honest and correct (MT 59:9's shift is a person shift, not an addressee change), but the register belongs outside row prose.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: restate the disclosure substantively (the signal at the front seam is a grammatical person shift into first-person-plural confession, not a change of addressee) without naming the field.

findings.claim: The rear seam at 61:3 | 61:4 rests on a 'changed subject' that MT 61:4 never states, and the row's own wording concedes the construction runs on across the seam.
findings.grounds: The row argues 'Isa.61.4 opens a further waw-plus-perfect clause with a changed subject ... distinct from the mourners just named'. MT 61:4 supplies no nominal subject at all — וּבָנוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) and וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) are bare third-person-plural forms whose nearest antecedent is the plural referent named one clause earlier at וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵילֵ֣י הַצֶּ֔דֶק (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier). The row itself calls 61:4 'a FURTHER waw-plus-perfect clause', i.e. the same construction that closes 61:3, which argues continuity across the seam; and the rejected_alternative's ground, 'Isa.61.4 opens a new finite-verb clause', is non-discriminating because the row has already identified 61:3's own close as a finite waw-plus-perfect clause. A stronger, unused ground stands in the row's own span: the first-person commission voice of 61:1-61:3 has no counterpart from 61:4 onward.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): re-argue the rear seam from the first-person commissioned-speaker frame that ends at 61:3 against the subjectless third-person report opening at MT 61:4, drop the unstated-referent claim, and re-cut rejected_alternative on the replacement warrant — noting that observed_substrate_signals, unit_type and confidence are dependent fields of any driver swap.

findings.claim: observed_substrate_signals records servant_song.referent_held_question for a span the row itself shows carries no servant vocabulary and that is not one of the book's staged servant-song candidate zones.
findings.grounds: The row states that 'this unit's own bytes lack the eved-root vocabulary that anchors the book's servant census', which re-derives from MT 61:1-61:3 (no eved-family token stands in those three verses). The held-question about the anointed speaker's identity is correctly left open, but the signal key asserts a servant-song class observed in bytes that do not carry its lexical anchor.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: keep the prose held-question disclosure and drop or re-key the servant_song.* entry to a class whose device actually stands in the row's own bytes.

findings.claim: The row states no tier-1 signal at its own front seam and never engages the preceding verse's bytes.
findings.grounds: The whole front-seam argument is 'A finite third-person-plural clause, “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4), matching וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), opens a report of the community's restoration' — an assertion that the clause opens a unit, with no stated reason why it does. MT 61:3 is never quoted, never named and carries no entry in boundary_evidence_refs, yet its own close is a finite waw-plus-perfect clause too, וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵילֵ֣י הַצֶּ֔דֶק מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), so the cited construction does not discriminate the seam. No vocative, imperative onset, messenger frame, wayyiqtol onset or addressee change stands at MT 61:4, and no parashah mark falls at this seam in the inventory.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): argue the front seam against MT 61:3's own bytes — the first-person commissioned-speaker frame closing there versus the subjectless third-person restoration report opening at MT 61:4 — and add oshb:Isa.61.3 to boundary_evidence_refs; observed_substrate_signals, rejected_alternative and confidence are dependent fields of the added driver.

findings.claim: The rear-seam driver — a Hebrew form-class claim about MT 61:10 — is carried on the English witness alone.
findings.grounds: The row closes at 61:9 'before Isa.61.10 opens with a fresh first-person voice, “I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh!” (web:Isa.61.10)'. The Hebrew that carries the claim, שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier), is never spliced and oshb:Isa.61.10 is absent from boundary_evidence_refs, which otherwise pairs an oshb ref with every web ref it cites. The claim is byte-true, and the book-order neighbor row splices exactly this run at byte tier for the same seam.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: splice שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) beside the WEB citation and add oshb:Isa.61.10 to boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: The row's sole front-seam signal, a first-person resolve onset, does not discriminate the seam and is neither spliced nor disclosed as continuous across it.
findings.grounds: The row opens 'A first-person resolve opens the unit' and records oracle_frame.first_person_resolve_onset as its only observed signal, but the first-person-singular voice is already running in the immediately preceding verses: שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) with נַפְשִׁי֙ and בֵּֽאלֹהַ֔י (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier). The book-order neighbor row states this explicitly for the same seam ('the first-person-singular voice itself runs on unbroken ... rather than by any change in speaker or person'); this row discloses no cross-seam continuity at its own front seam. The resolve itself is also never spliced — the only Hebrew given at that verse, צִדְקָ֔הּ וִישׁוּעָתָ֖הּ (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier), is the third-person Zion phrase from the verse's second half, while the resolve verbs לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה and לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier) are absent from the row.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): splice לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה and לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier) as the named onset, disclose that the first-person-singular voice straddles the front seam from oshb:Isa.61.10, and re-state what actually discriminates the seam (the lamed-purpose Zion/Jerusalem vow) — observed_substrate_signals and confidence are dependent fields of that restatement.

findings.claim: The front-seam driver is a vocative in apposition to an addressee that runs on unbroken across the seam, and that continuity is undisclosed in this row.
findings.grounds: The row argues 'An explicit vocative and a new first-person divine act open the unit'. The vocative stands as the third token of MT 62:6, עַל חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier), in apposition to a second-person-feminine-singular addressee already running from MT 62:2 — צִדְקֵ֔ךְ and כְּבוֹדֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier) — through עָלַ֖יִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.5, byte tier) at the preceding unit's own close. It therefore names the same addressee rather than opening a fresh one, and the book-order neighbor row argues this same seam as marked 'not by any change of addressee, speaker, or person'. This row discloses addressee alternation inside its span but not the unbroken address across its own front seam.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): disclose that the second-person-feminine-singular address straddles the front seam from MT 62:2 onward, and re-state the onset as a vocative re-address plus a new completed first-person divine act rather than as a fresh vocative addressee; observed_substrate_signals and confidence are dependent fields.

findings.claim: The rear seam at 62:9 | 62:10 is argued on exactly the ground the book-order neighbor row rejects for the same seam.
findings.grounds: This row closes because 'Isa.62.10 opens a fresh plural-imperative summons ... addressed to an unnamed group rather than continuing the charge just laid on the watchmen'. The neighbor row opening at 62:10 rejects that ground in terms: 'The preceding verses already command an addressed-plural group, the posted watchmen; the turn at this unit's own onset is not a shift to an unnamed addressee but a shift in content', and its rejected_alternative repeats 'not because it addresses an unnamed group'. The bytes support the neighbor: MT 62:6-62:7 already charge a plural addressee at אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) and וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.62.7, byte tier), so the addressee of the summons is no more unnamed at 62:10 than at 62:6.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): re-argue the rear seam on the verse-initial doubled imperative and the content turn to highway preparation, dropping the 'unnamed group' ground so the seam is argued compatibly from both sides.

findings.claim: The rear-seam driver — a Hebrew form-class claim about MT 62:10 — is carried on the English witness alone.
findings.grounds: The row calls 62:10 'a fresh plural-imperative summons' and cites only web:Isa.62.10; the Hebrew that carries the claim, עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier), is never spliced and oshb:Isa.62.10 is absent from boundary_evidence_refs, which pairs an oshb ref with every other web ref it cites. The claim is byte-true, and the book-order neighbor row splices exactly this run at byte tier for the same seam.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: splice עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier) beside the WEB citation and add oshb:Isa.62.10 to boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: The rear-seam warrant is byte-false: MT 63:7 does not open a first-person-plural recital, and no change of grammatical person occurs across the seam.
findings.grounds: The row ends its span 'because 63:7 pivots to a different speaker and a different speech-act: a first-person-plural recital of Yahweh's mercies replaces the divine warrior's own first-person report'. MT 63:7's speech-act verb is first-person SINGULAR: חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), matched by the English witness's 'I will tell of the loving kindnesses of Yahweh' (web:Isa.63.7); the verse's only plural first-person element is the object suffix on גְּמָלָ֖נוּ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier). The preceding unit closes in first-person singular as well — וְאָב֤וּס עַמִּים֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י (oshb:Isa.63.6, byte tier) — so the person is unchanged across the seam. The book-order neighbor row states this correctly and oppositely ('a first-person-singular self-announcing speech-act verb ... the same grammatical person as the preceding unit's own divine-warrior voice, so the seam is marked by the change in speech-act, not by any change of person'). The row also carries no oshb:Isa.63.7 entry and no splice for the verse its rear seam turns on, and ships at confidence 'high' with frontier_flag_considered false.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement; the seam itself survives on the speech-act change and the tier-3 SAMEKH already disclosed at MT 63:6): delete the 'first-person-plural recital' ground, re-argue the seam as a change of speech-act at unchanged grammatical person, splice חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), add oshb:Isa.63.7 to boundary_evidence_refs, and re-test confidence and frontier_flag now that the person-shift ground is withdrawn.

findings.claim: The row's prose carries two bare, witness-unqualified chapter-and-verse coordinates inside offset zone B, where the same numerals denote different verses in the two witnesses.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale says the theophany imagery continues 'past the split (fire kindling brushwood, the nations trembling, mountains quaking again at 64:2-3)' and strongest_rejected_alternative says 'the confessional turn at 64:5'. Neither carries a witness prefix or a numeric qualifier. The content named is WEB-numbered: the mountain-quaking report is web:Isa.64.3 = oshb:Isa.64.2, %s (oshb:Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3, byte tier), while oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4 is instead the incomparability affirmation; and the confession verse is web:Isa.64.5 = oshb:Isa.64.4. The row's own structured refs and device_notes do carry the duals, so the prose is inconsistent with the row's own disclosure standard on the book's single split-verse row.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: qualify both prose coordinates (web:Isa.64.2-Isa.64.3 (MT 64:1-64:2) and web:Isa.64.5 (MT 64:4)) to match the disclosure already used elsewhere in the row.

findings.claim: The rear-seam warrant presents the confessional turn as opening web:Isa.64.5, but that verse opens on continuing second-person praise; the confession begins only after the verse's own caesura.
findings.grounds: The row closes 'immediately before the confessional turn “Behold, you were angry, and we sinned.” (web:Isa.64.5) opens a different speech-act'. web:Isa.64.5 = oshb:Isa.64.4, whose first half is %s (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier), rendered 'You meet him who rejoices and does righteousness, those who remember you in your ways.' (web:Isa.64.5 = oshb:Isa.64.4) — second-person address continuing the preceding material; the self-accusation %s (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier) stands only after that verse's own athnach at %s (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier). The book-order neighbor row discloses this mid-verse onset explicitly; this row does not, so its stated rhetorical-mode driver is presented as verse-initial when it is not.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement; web:Isa.64.4 = oshb:Isa.64.3 remains the last verse boundary available before the turn): disclose that the confessional turn stands mid-verse in oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, after that verse's own caesura, and state the seam as the nearest verse boundary before it.

findings.claim: The cross-split echo is given two different tier labels in one sentence, with no splice and no digit, and is keyed in observed_substrate_signals as a refrain the row itself declines to treat as a device.
findings.grounds: device_notes calls the same echo 'near-verbatim' and 'a byte-true echo'. Collation separates the two: מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ (oshb:Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.64.1, second half of the split verse, byte tier) stands byte-identical as the same run at oshb:Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3 — 2 verses book-wide — whereas the longer run including יָרַ֔דְתָּ (oshb:Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.64.1, second half of the split verse, byte tier) against יָרַ֕דְתָּ (oshb:Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3, byte tier) meets only from accent-stripped tier down (byte tier: 1 verse). No Hebrew is spliced for the claim and no digit is given. observed_substrate_signals meanwhile carries refrain.theophany_mountains_quake for a two-site echo that device_notes says is 'disclosed here rather than argued as a boundary'.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: splice מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ (oshb:Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.64.1, second half of the split verse, byte tier) with its 2-verse sweep digit and one tier label (byte tier), drop the conflicting 'near-verbatim' wording or attach it to the longer accent-stripped run, and re-key or drop the refrain.* signal.
